column1: # core/spec/divergent.tsv — the core-level parity debt, one row per divergence.
# One row per expression, tab-separated:  expr <TAB> go <TAB> ts <TAB> note
# Same comment and escaping rules as the other core/spec files, and the same
# two-runner discipline: core/go/corespec_test.go asserts the `go` column and
# core/ts/src/corespec.test.ts asserts the `ts` column, so both suites stay
# green while the difference stays PINNED. If either engine moves, its column
# fails and the row is re-examined rather than silently re-baselined. Each
# runner also FAILS a row whose go and ts columns are EQUAL — a fixed
# divergence must MOVE to the spec file it belongs in, or this stops being an
# honest debt list.
# SHRINK-ONLY, exactly as parser/spec/divergent.tsv is.
# WHERE THESE CAME FROM. The 1808-row engine crossdiff has been green
# throughout, and so has every core/spec row. None of these were visible to
# either, because a differential that hard-fails only when both engines
# SUCCEED with different values cannot see two engines that both fail, and
# because no source in eng/spec builds the shapes below. They were found by
# sweeping core/ts's UNCOVERED regions — the parser half of this program
# established that an uncovered branch in one port is where a divergence
# hides, and this file is that finding applied to core.
# The `go` column is the reference by CONVENTION, not by proof. Two of the
# five original parser-side divergence classes turned out to have Go wrong.
# Read design/CORE-TS-DIVERGENCES.1.md before assuming which side moves.
# WHAT HAS CLOSED. The port's two halves landed on 2026-11-27 and their rows
# moved to the spec files their rules are pinned in: the unifier, resolution
# and rendering half to unify.tsv, data.tsv, canon.tsv and dispatch.tsv; the
# engine half — the call frame and its return check, a function VALUE's
# dispatch, `name/v`, `name/u`, the word `end`, a def-bound list, an
# unmatched `(` — to dispatch.tsv, with function identity in unify.tsv.
# What is left below is what core/ts does not have at all — closures and
# driven loops — one recorded kernel defect (NUR392), pinned as the kernel
# has it, and, last, what a differential search found once the engine half
# had closed.
# --- ANONYMOUS functions, built at run time -----------------------------------
# `afn n [q body… ]` is the closure fixture: it builds a one-parameter
# function where it stands, as the language's own `afn` does (README). The
# function a NATIVE returns is stepped like any result, so it is called with
# what follows; with nothing it can take beside it, an anonymous function is
# simply a value — never uncalled_function, which is a NAMED function's
# error. A group that collapses to a function alone places it.
run afn n [q addq n 1 ]
column4: DATA: core/ts has no closures — its fixture registers no `afn`, and the engine keeps no frame baseline and no captured bindings — so the word is unknown there.

column1: # --- CLOSURES: a function keeps the frame it was built in ------------------
# `outer x` builds `n ↦ n + x` in its own frame and returns it. A function a
# FRAME returns is a value — it is not called with what follows — so the rows
# hand it to `bothq`, which answers it, and THAT result is called. By then
# `outer`'s frame is gone: the closure reads the `x` it captured, and reads
# it in preference to a global `x` bound since. A parameter is the call's,
# never a capture. A name bound at the top level is not captured either: it
# is read when the body runs, and refused then if it is not bound.
run def outer fn( x Integer Any [ afn n [q addq n x ] ] ) ; bothq 1 ( outer 10 ) 5

column1: # --- DRIVEN LOOPS: a body runs in a region of its own -------------------------
# `eachq xs [q body… ]` is the loop fixture: an iteration per element, the
# element the region's one input, and EVERYTHING a region leaves collected,
# in order, into the one list the loop answers. The body's stack is its
# input — nothing beneath the loop's word is in its sight (`depthq` answers
# 1, and `addq` cannot reach the 7 and 8). An empty body leaves its input;
# an empty list runs no body at all. A body's error is the loop's.
run eachq [q 1 2 3 ] [q negq ]

column1: # --- what a differential search found once the ENGINE half had closed --------
# The six causes the engine half was given are closed. A Go-against-TS search
# over the same fixture words then turned these up: each is a mechanism
# core/go has and core/ts does not, and none is one of the six. They are
# pinned so that the ledger says so. (The Lean model answers every one as Go
# does.)
# The forward barrier's COMMIT half. core/ts strands a parked word at a
# function word only when it has claimed NOTHING — engine.ts's
# strandedForwardError says why the subset stops there. One that has claimed
# part of its plan waits through, and is fed the boundary word's result.
run bothq 1 negq 5
column4: CODE: the strict forward barrier's commit half is not ported — a parked word that has collected part of its plan is stranded in Go when a function word begins its own dispatch; core/ts waits through and takes that word's result.

A `/u` word is a function word like any other: the modifier does not make it an argument.

column1: # A TYPE-ARG slot plans a WORD. Go's plan counts the word after `tyq` as its
# forward argument — a name may be bound to a type — so an unbound name is
# undefined_word and a function word strands the collection. core/ts plans
# only what is a type already: `tyq` dispatches on what the stack holds, or
# fails for want of it, and the word runs on its own.
run tyq zzz
column4: CODE: a type-arg slot plans the word after it in Go, so the unbound name is stepped and is undefined; core/ts does not plan a word there and fails the dispatch for want of an argument.

column1: # An ORPHANED collection is re-dispatched when the run ends, with what it
# collected and the stack beneath it (core/go resolveOrphanedForwards).
# core/ts refuses any collection the end of the run finds unfilled.
run 1 bothq __pa true
column4: CODE: Go re-dispatches a collection the run's end finds unfilled — what it collected, then the stack — so `bothq` takes the 1 beneath it; core/ts refuses the unfilled collection.

column4: CODE: Go re-dispatches a collection the run's end finds unfilled — what it collected, then the stack — so `bothq` takes the pending list, whose evaluation faults; core/ts refuses the unfilled collection.

column1: # A function VALUE parks its collection like a word in Go, so an
# engine-internal `__` word after it is stepped and passed over; core/ts
# matches a boru-bodied function where it stands, and counts the `__` word as
# an argument it could not take.
run fn( n Any Any [ negq n ] ) __pa
column4: CODE: Go parks a function value's collection, steps the engine-internal word and, with nothing left, leaves the function as a value; core/ts matches it where it stands and counts the `__` word as a refused argument.

column1: run fn( n Any Any [ negq n ] ) __pa 5
column4: CODE: Go parks a function value's collection, steps the engine-internal word and collects the 5 after it; core/ts matches it where it stands and counts the `__` word as a refused argument.

column1: # A FRAME's results are stepped again where the call stood: core/go splices
# the frame into the tape. core/ts's frame is a run of its own and its
# residual is placed, so a raw WORD a body hands back is called in Go and
# carried in core/ts.
run def inc fn( n Any Any [ n ] ) ; def h negq ; inc h
column4: CODE: a frame's residual is re-stepped in Go, so the word `negq` the body hands back is called, with nothing; core/ts places a frame's residual and carries the word.

column1: # The `undef` FIXTURE reaches further in Go: a native word is a binding
# there, and `undef` removes it. core/ts keeps natives apart from the def
# stack, and its fixture pops only a def.
run undef negq ; negq 2
column4: DATA: a native word is a binding `undef` can remove in core/go; core/ts keeps natives apart from the def stack, so the word is still there.

column1: # --- `/uv` in a boru-bodied call's forward window ------------------------------
# The kernel places a `/uv` wrapper without delivering it (NUR390), and the
# call that was waiting goes on to collect the NEXT value. core/ts treats
# the `/uv` word as a function word that strands the waiting call. These rows
# sit on NUR390's accident and will move when it is ruled on.
run def f fn( n Any Any [ n ] ) ; f f/uv 5
column4: CODE: core/ts strands a boru-bodied call that meets a `/uv` word in its forward window; Go places the wrapper and lets the call collect what follows (NUR390).
